partners.mechanism_chain: PHKA2 (HGNC:9038) —DISRUPTS→ Phosphorylase kinase complex activity (GO:0004073); PHKG2 (HGNC:9041) —DISRUPTS→ Phosphorylase kinase complex activity (GO:0004073); Phosphorylase kinase complex activity (GO:0004073) —DECREASES→ Glycogenolysis (GO:0005977); Phosphorylase kinase complex activity (GO:0004073) —DECREASES→ Gluconeogenesis (GO:0006094); Glycogenolysis (GO:0005977) —DECREASES→ Glucose (CHEBI:17234); Gluconeogenesis (GO:0006094) —DECREASES→ Glucose (CHEBI:17234); Glycogenolysis (GO:0005977) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0002240); Gluconeogenesis (GO:0006094) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001257). Mutations in PHKA2 (GSD IXa1) and PHKG2 (GSD IXc) lead to reduced activity of the phosphorylase kinase complex, which is essential for both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Impaired glycogenolysis results in the inability to mobilize glucose stores, contributing to hypoglycemia and potentially hepatomegaly due to glycogen accumulation. Impaired gluconeogenesis further exacerbates hypoglycemia. The shared disruption of the phosphorylase kinase complex and its downstream metabolic pathways (glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis) explains the overlapping phenotypes.

**Proposed mechanism:** PHKA2 (HGNC:8891) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogenolysis (GO:0005977); Glycogenolysis (GO:0005977) —DECREASES→ Calcium signaling (GO:0005886); Calcium signaling (GO:0005886) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0006950); CALM1 (HGNC:1694) —INCREASES→ Calcium signaling (GO:0005886); Calcium signaling (GO:0005886) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0006950); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0006950) —LEADS_TO→ Glycogen storage disease IXa1 (MONDO:0010598); Cardiac muscle contraction (GO:0006950) —LEADS_TO→ Long QT syndrome 14 (MONDO:0014548). Loss-of-function mutations in PHKA2 impair glycogenolysis, which can indirectly affect cellular energy homeostasis and potentially calcium handling in cardiomyocytes. Gain-of-function mutations in CALM1 directly dysregulate calcium signaling, leading to prolonged action potentials and arrhythmias. Both pathways converge on the disruption of normal cardiac muscle contraction.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that genetic variants in PHKA2 do not lead to any detectable alteration in cardiac function or calcium handling in vitro or in vivo, or that variants in CALM1 do not affect cardiac electrophysiology or contractility. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a high frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants in both PHKA2 and CALM1 associated with these specific diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could lead to novel therapeutic strategies. For GSD IXa1, interventions aimed at supporting cardiac energy metabolism or modulating calcium handling might be beneficial. For LQTS14, insights from metabolic pathways could potentially inform combination therapies, although the primary focus remains on ion channel function. Both highlight the critical role of integrated cellular processes in cardiac health.
